primary_findings.conclusion: Both installed MacOSX26.5 and MacOSX15.4 SDK getrusage.2 documents specify ru_maxrss in bytes. Their ps.1 documents specify rss in1024-byte units. Retain raw values and explicit conversion metadata; do not apply a Linux multiplier to Darwin ru_maxrss.

primary_findings.conclusion: At the fixed XNU commit, calcru assigns Mach resident_size_max directly to ru_maxrss. The corresponding Mach task-info header defines resident_size_max in bytes. The reviewed implementation therefore supports byte units for SELF and the same unscaled field transported through wait4.

Apple's older online archived getrusage manual instead specifies kilobytes and carries a1993 BSD date. This conflicts with the installed SDK wording. Preserve the discrepancy; the archive is not the authority for current runtime conversion. Exact host/runtime pins and bounded prospective calibration remain necessary.

At the fixed XNU commit, ruadd adds user/system time and the later counters, but combines ru_maxrss by maximum. The resource header starts the additive counter range after ru_maxrss. RUSAGE_CHILDREN copies the accumulated p_cru; SELF obtains p_ru after current-task accounting.

At this commit, exit folds accumulated child usage into the saved terminal record. wait4 copies that record, then ordinary reaping rolls it into the waiting parent's child accumulator. A directly awaited child can therefore return a descendant-inclusive RSS maximum. The rollup is conditional on ordinary ownership/reaping and SIGCHLD handling; live reparented or unaccounted descendants cannot be assumed covered.
primary_findings.supporting_manual: Local SDK wait.2 lines135-140 describes child-and-children resource usage; official older wait manual agrees on that scope.

inferences_for_future_source_review: A descendant-inclusive maximum is not a sum of simultaneous process RSS. Several concurrent children can jointly exceed their largest individual high-water mark.

After reaping the scientific owner, a wrapper's cumulative RUSAGE_CHILDREN RSS maximum includes that owner and rolled-up descendants. It cannot then be labeled ps-only memory. The previously saved wrapper source does exactly this; that statement explains its conservative overlapping scopes but changes no historical result.

The difference of two cumulative maxima does not recover the intervening observer's peak: a smaller observer may produce a zero difference. Similarly, a terminal max and a known descendant max cannot uniquely recover the exiting parent's own peak.

A separate direct wait4 record for each verified leaf observer can provide its own terminal scope. Sequentiality must be established per caller; observers owned by different nested callers may overlap and must be accounted separately.

A terminal child maximum may conservatively upper-bound that child's SELF high-water value while overlapping descendants. Any prospective adapter using it must explicitly state the bound and keep separate owned descendant coverage; it must not call the value exact simultaneous tree memory.

Summing justified per-process RSS/high-water bounds is conservative and can count shared pages more than once. Sampling simultaneous RSS does not by itself bound missed short-lived peaks. No hard OS memory-cap enforcement is established by these retrospective records.

Current-task high-water semantics do not establish full fork/exec lifecycle coverage without reviewing the pinned runtime and process topology. Complete import/startup/hash/serialization/close/exit/reap clocks remain separate obligations.
